rv.q: Yet, there’s so much more to this than its admittedly clever toilet humour and witty digs at everything from the Acts of Union to Scottish exceptionalism. It’s a history lesson, going all the way back to the Picts, and a portrait of a nation that has always been much more than its stereotypes.
It’s a pleasingly surreal tale about loneliness and loss, in other words, in a society where apps like Tinder seem to offer 30-year-olds like Joy their only hope of ever not being alone.
